the firm-fleshed, amber Deglet Noor and

Khadrawy, and Halawy are “soft” dates.
“Dry” varieties contain relatively little
moisture when ripe.  Thus, the term “dry”
does not mean “dehydrated” or “dried.”
Origin & botanical facts
Dates originated somewhere in the desert
area that stretches from India to North
Africa.  Cultivation seems to have begun
at least 8,000 years ago, when settlement
began along the Jordan River and around
the Dead Sea.  Archaeological evidence
indicates that cultivation of dates was well
established by 3000 B.C. in what is now
Iraq.
The northern coastal region of the
Middle East was originally called
Phoenicia, a name that may be the source
of the early Greek term for the date,
phoenix.  The word “date” appears to
